quote: I've had the roof repaired. And I think it's as good as it's gonna get for the next twenty years.
stewart_read: Customer proactively resolves the exact objection that stalled her prior design — a strong buy signal Randy should have explicitly acknowledged and anchored.
coaching_implication: Reflect this back verbally ('great, that clears the roof concern we had last time') to reinforce her own resolution and build confidence before jumping to scheduling.

quote: This was gonna be a program where I I would be you you would be the owner or you would rent it out to somebody, and I didn't have to pay for anything.
stewart_read: Melanie is describing what sounds like a PPA/lease/TPO structure and asking for confirmation of the offer; Randy neither confirms, corrects, nor bridges to a specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Randy may be deliberately avoiding a technical/financial answer to stay in scope — but he doesn't redirect her to the specialist either, so it reads as a gap, not a strategic scope-hold.
coaching_implication: Use the escape hatch explicitly: 'great question — that's exactly what the specialist will walk through tomorrow' instead of the filler agreement.

quote: Yeah. I'm yeah. Sounds like Yeah. Yeah. What we're still offering.
stewart_read: A cluster of filler affirmations with no actual content — Randy doesn't confirm, correct, or clarify the ownership model Melanie just described.
coaching_implication: Replace filler agreement with a specific redirect line to avoid implying confirmation of terms he hasn't verified.

quote: 4PM. 4PM sounds great. Yep. Yep. Okay. Awesome.
stewart_read: Time is locked, but Randy skips the full button-up (no one-hour block, no computer/no-driving instruction, no 'is that fair' handshake) before moving to close.
coaching_implication: Even on a fast, warm re-book, run the full button-up checklist — it protects show rate regardless of how easy the booking felt.

quote: I'll just send you a confirmation text with the date and time of the meeting.
stewart_read: Call ends without the verbal handshake or expectation-setting (driving/computer instruction), relying only on a text promise.
coaching_implication: Add 'is that fair?' and the no-driving/computer instruction before signing off, even on short warm calls.

quote: It looks like we might have already, met with you.
stewart_read: Randy acknowledges the prior design/meeting but never asks what was shown, who ran it, or why it didn't close beyond the roof issue.
alternative_hypothesis: The call is short and moves fast because Randy may be relying on visible CRM notes rather than needing to re-ask — but the transcript shows no evidence he actually reviewed what was previously proposed.
coaching_implication: Ask one clarifying question about the prior design/specialist outcome before re-booking, to hand the closer real context instead of a blank slate.
